root_cause.text: The driver incorrectly tied device-managed resources (SPI controller, driver data, buffers) to the parent USB device's lifetime instead of the USB interface's lifetime, causing resource leaks when the driver is unbound from the interface without the physical device being disconnected.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes all `devm_spi_alloc_host`, `devm_kzalloc` calls from `&udev->dev` to `&intf->dev`, ensuring resources are released on driver unbind rather than persisting until the USB device is removed. The commit message explicitly states this fixes devres lifetime issues.

bic_trace_step.reason: In ch341_probe(), device-managed resources (SPI controller via devm_spi_alloc_master, RX and TX buffers via devm_kzalloc) are allocated using the parent USB device (&udev->dev) instead of the USB interface (&intf->dev). This ties resource lifetimes to the USB device, not the interface. When the driver is unbound from the interface (e.g., module unbind) while the physical USB device remains connected, these devm resources are not freed, causing a leak. The disconnect() function only manually frees the URB but does not free the devm-allocated resources, confirming the vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The probe function uses devm_spi_alloc_master(&udev->dev, ...) and devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, ...) to allocate resources, tying them to the parent USB device (udev->dev) instead of the USB interface (&intf->dev).
